source_references.title: Prompt injection attacks against GPT-3
source_references.author: Simon Willison
source_references.evidence_scope: Defines prompt injection as a class of attacks caused by mixing trusted application prompts with attacker-controlled natural-language instructions.
source_references.notes: Reference metadata only; the source body is not copied into this repository.

source_references.title: The Dual LLM pattern for building AI assistants that can resist prompt injection
source_references.author: Simon Willison
source_references.evidence_scope: Proposes privileged and quarantined model roles plus a non-model controller; identifies outbound HTTP, links, remote images, repeated-approval fatigue, and unsafe chaining as concrete risks; and states explicit limitations of the pattern.
source_references.notes: Reference metadata only; the source body is not copied into this repository.

source_references.title: Delimiters won’t save you from prompt injection
source_references.author: Simon Willison
source_references.evidence_scope: Demonstrates why delimiter-only prompt defenses do not create a reliable security boundary against adversarial instructions.
source_references.notes: Reference metadata only; the source body and demonstration prompts are not copied into this repository.

source_references.title: CaMeL offers a promising new direction for mitigating prompt injection attacks
source_references.author: Simon Willison
source_references.evidence_scope: Explains how attacker-influenced recipient data defeats the earlier Dual LLM proposal; favors capability tracking, data-flow policy, and deterministic system design over probabilistic filtering; and records user-fatigue limitations.
source_references.notes: Reference metadata and bounded paraphrase only; neither the article nor the reviewed paper is copied into this repository.

source_references.title: The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication
source_references.author: Simon Willison
source_references.evidence_scope: Identifies the high-risk combination of private data, untrusted content, and external communication; names APIs, image loads, and user-clicked links as outbound channels; and states that prompt-only guardrails are not reliable protection.
source_references.notes: Reference metadata only; the source body and diagram are not copied into this repository.

principles.statement: Treat trusted instructions and untrusted content as different security domains instead of relying on an LLM to distinguish them reliably in one token stream.
principles.evidence_note: Both authored posts identify the mixing of trusted instructions and untrusted text as the root security problem.
context_dependencies: LLM applications that ingest content not controlled by the operator

principles.statement: Do not combine private-data access, exposure to untrusted content, and external communication unless the architecture removes a capability or enforces a reliable boundary.
principles.evidence_note: The authored post explicitly identifies this three-part combination as enabling data theft and recommends avoiding it.
context_dependencies: Tool-using LLM systems with access to non-public information

principles.statement: Prefer deterministic capability and data-flow enforcement around models to probabilistic model-based attack detection for consequential security decisions.
principles.evidence_note: The authored sources reject percentage-based filtering as an adequate application-security guarantee and favor system-level constraints.
context_dependencies: Adversarial environments where one successful bypass can cause material harm

signature_moves.statement: Process untrusted content in a quarantined component without tool authority, and prevent its free-form output from reaching a privileged planner.
signature_moves.evidence_note: The Dual LLM proposal directly specifies privileged and quarantined roles plus a non-model controller that preserves this boundary.
context_dependencies: Assistants that must inspect attacker-influenceable documents, email, web pages, or images

signature_moves.statement: Track the provenance of values derived from untrusted content and apply explicit policy before those values can parameterize consequential actions.
signature_moves.evidence_note: The CaMeL review highlights capability tags, data-flow tracking, and action policies as the promising advance over a simple two-model split.
context_dependencies: Agent workflows where retrieved data supplies recipients, paths, commands, or other action parameters

signature_moves.statement: Inventory and restrict every outbound channel, including API calls, links, and remotely loaded media, when a model can access sensitive data.
signature_moves.evidence_note: The authored sources enumerate direct and indirect communication mechanisms that can carry exfiltrated data.
context_dependencies: Interfaces that render model-produced URLs, images, messages, or tool calls

likely_objections.statement: A security claim based only on system prompts, delimiters, or a model-based detector does not establish a reliable adversarial boundary.
likely_objections.evidence_note: The authored sources demonstrate delimiter bypass and explain why probabilistic detection leaves exploitable failures.
context_dependencies: Security-sensitive systems exposed to attacker-controlled input

likely_objections.statement: A two-model split alone is insufficient when untrusted data can still determine privileged action parameters such as a message recipient.
likely_objections.evidence_note: The 2025 post explicitly updates the earlier proposal with a concrete confused-deputy flaw and a stronger data-flow design.
context_dependencies: Systems implementing the 2023 Dual LLM pattern

likely_objections.statement: Human approval is not a complete mitigation when frequent prompts train users to approve requests without meaningful scrutiny.
likely_objections.evidence_note: Both authored posts explicitly identify dialog or user fatigue as a limitation of approval-based controls.
context_dependencies: High-frequency workflows that require repeated user authorization

anti_patterns.statement: Giving one agent private data, untrusted inputs, and unrestricted outbound communication creates an unacceptable exfiltration path.
anti_patterns.evidence_note: This is the bounded system configuration identified in the authored lethal-trifecta analysis.
context_dependencies: General-purpose agents assembled from independently trusted tools

anti_patterns.statement: Rendering arbitrary model-generated links or remote images can turn an apparently passive response into a data-exfiltration channel.
anti_patterns.evidence_note: The authored analysis describes links and image loads as outbound channels that need explicit control.
context_dependencies: User interfaces that automatically render or encourage opening model-produced resources

anti_patterns.statement: Treating a proposed prompt-injection mitigation as complete without adversarial validation and documented residual limitations creates false certainty.
anti_patterns.evidence_note: This inference follows from the explicit self-critique of the 2023 design and the 2025 discussion of CaMeL's remaining limitations.
anti_patterns.inference_basis: The later source revises a previously proposed mitigation and preserves explicit caveats, supporting a bounded expectation of continued adversarial review rather than permanence.
context_dependencies: Design reviews that claim prompt-injection resistance
Apply this lens to LLM applications and agents that process attacker-influenceable content or use tools.
Use it as an application-security perspective, not as a general software architecture or machine-learning quality profile.
Reassess after the validity window because agent capabilities and prompt-injection mitigations are changing rapidly.
